symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled units in the stated finite-sample frontier.

symbols.name: \Delta_0
symbols.def: A fixed upper bound on the released radial bin width.

symbols.name: \Delta
symbols.def: The known width of every floor-rounded radial bin.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The known common constant in the two side-specific point-anchored boundary envelopes.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The prescribed error probability for honest confidence intervals.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: The target point, normalized to \(b=(0,0)\).

symbols.name: e_1
symbols.def: The unit vector \(e_1=(1,0)\) used only to specify the uniform half-disc least-favorable subclass.

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1\}\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The raw location score, which is sampled but not released to the analyst.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=\lVert X-b\rVert_2\).

symbols.name: Y(0)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y(1)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A one-unit law for the latent score and potential outcomes; treatment and the observed outcome are induced by sharp assignment and consistency.

symbols.name: Q_\Delta
symbols.def: \(Q_\Delta(r)=\Delta\lfloor r/\Delta\rfloor\).

symbols.name: \rho_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(\rho_{n,\Delta}=\max\{h_n,\Delta\}\).

symbols.name: K_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(K_{n,\Delta}=\lceil h_n/\Delta\rceil\).

symbols.name: H_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(H_{n,\Delta}=K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\).

symbols.name: I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{n,\gamma}(s)
symbols.def: For any positive integer trial count \(k\), \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\gamma}(s)\) is the equal-tailed exact \(1-\gamma\) binomial confidence interval after \(s\) successes in \(k\) trials.

symbols.name: c_0
symbols.def: A fixed class constant lower-bounding each side probability in a radius-\(H\) neighborhood by \(c_0H^2\).

symbols.name: \mathcal X_{t,P}
symbols.def: The known Borel partition satisfies \(\mathcal X_{0,P}\cap\mathcal X_{1,P}=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal X_{0,P}\cup\mathcal X_{1,P}=\mathcal D\); the local-mass condition implies that \(b\) lies in the closure of both sides.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The realized outcome under the sharp assignment.

symbols.name: Z_\Delta
symbols.def: \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\); neither \(X\), the polar angle, nor raw \(R\) is observed.

symbols.name: S_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(S_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}Y_i\).

symbols.name: \mathcal T_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: All law-independent estimators measurable with respect to the released sample only.

symbols.name: N_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The observed-count ratio with fixed zero-count fallback constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bin\text{-}aware\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

symbols.name: C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
symbols.def: The conditional-count exact-binomial interval with sidewise spatial Lipschitz enlargement constructed in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\).

symbols.name: \theta_t
symbols.def: The number in \([0,1]\) anchoring side \(t\) at the fixed boundary point \(b\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_L
symbols.type: unknown-design bivariate Bernoulli point-anchored boundary law class
symbols.def: The one-unit full-data laws with the stated known side partition, two-sided quadratic local mass, Bernoulli outcomes, consistency, and side-specific point-anchored envelopes.

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The explicit embedded uniform-half-disc pair constructed in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).
symbols.role: joint minimax and honest-length lower certificate

symbols.name: \mu_t
symbols.def: \(\mu_t(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point, with the declared boundary value \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).
symbols.role: outcome regression and boundary anchor carrier

symbols.name: m_t
symbols.type: radial profile for constructed least-favorable laws
symbols.sig: \([0,1]\to[1/4,3/4]\) on the embedded uniform half-disc subclass
symbols.def: For a constructed radial law, \(m_t(r)\) denotes the profile satisfying \(\mu_t(x)=m_t(\lVert x-b\rVert_2)\); it is not a restriction on every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).

symbols.name: \tau_P(b)
symbols.def: \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0=\mu_1(b)-\mu_0(b)\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}
symbols.def: The squared risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The interval class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The width criterion constructed in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}width}\).

symbols.name: P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}
symbols.def: The two bivariate laws constructed in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).
symbols.role: exact nonidentification witness in a least-favorable subclass

assumptions.condition: \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
For the fixed class constant \(c_0\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\) for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).
There is a known Borel side partition \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) of \(\mathcal D\) such that \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely under \(P\).

standard.name: sharp assignment across a known bivariate boundary

assumptions.condition:
For every \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) satisfying \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\),
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2.
\]

definitions.name: Unknown-design bivariate Bernoulli point-anchored boundary class
definitions.construction:
\(\mathcal P_L\) is the set of one-unit laws \(P\) such that \(P_X(\mathcal D)=1\); for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(H\in(0,1/2]\), \(\mathbb P_P(T=t,\lVert X-b\rVert_2<H)\geq c_0H^2\); \((\mathcal X_{0,P},\mathcal X_{1,P})\) is a known Borel partition of \(\mathcal D\) and \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\) almost surely; \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\) almost surely; for each \(t\), \(Y(t)\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_t(x))\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\); and the point-anchored envelope
\[
 |\mu_t(x)-\theta_t|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
\]
holds for every \(t\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every side-\(t\) point \(x\) of radius at most \(1/2\), where \(\theta_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\).  The sampling condition \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) is imposed on the sample and is not a member property of a one-unit law.

definitions.name: Rounded-radius observation experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{n,\Delta}(P)=\mathcal L_P(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\),\quad Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,\Delta\lfloor R_i/\Delta\rfloor)\). The observation \(\sigma\)-field is exactly \(\sigma(Z_{\Delta,1},\ldots,Z_{\Delta,n})\); it excludes \(X_i\), angle, and raw \(R_i\).

definitions.name: Total bin-aware local-constant estimator
definitions.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{T_i=t,Q_\Delta(R_i)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=
 \begin{cases}
 \Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta}\right),&N_{t,n,\Delta}>0,\\
 1/2,&N_{t,n,\Delta}=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 H_{n,\Delta}=\Delta\left\lceil n^{-1/4}/\Delta\right\rceil,
\]
where \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) is Euclidean clipping, and set \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\).

definitions.name: Rounded-radius minimax risks
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b)|\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}=\inf_{\widetilde\tau\in\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_P(b))^2]\).

definitions.name: Honest closed bounded confidence-interval class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)=\{C:C\text{ is a closed bounded interval-valued, }\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\text{-measurable map and }\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb P_P(\tau_P(b)\in C)\geq1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Bias-enlarged conditional-count exact-binomial interval
definitions.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set \([\ell_t,u_t]=[0,1]\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), and set \([\ell_t,u_t]=I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{N_{t,n,\Delta},\alpha/2}(S_{t,n,\Delta})\) when \(N_{t,n,\Delta}>0\).  With \(B_{n,\Delta}=LH_{n,\Delta}\), define the closed bounded interval
\[
 C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}
 =\bigl[\ell_1-u_0-2B_{n,\Delta},\ u_1-\ell_0+2B_{n,\Delta}\bigr].
\]

definitions.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc exact first-bin alias pair
definitions.construction:
For each sign, construct \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{\pm,\Delta}\) by drawing \(X\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D\), taking \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assigning \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal X_{1,P}\}\), and drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes given \(X\) with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}.
\]
Finally set \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), where \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) and \(c_L=\min\{L/8,1/16\}\).

definitions.name: Embedded uniform-half-disc joint lower handle
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}=(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta})\) denote the following pair.  Under both laws, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal X_{1,P}=\{x\in\mathcal D:e_1^{\top}(x-b)\geq0\}\), assignment is sharp, and the control mean is \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\) the treated mean is \(1/2\); under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\) it is
\[
 \frac12+\frac{c_L}{4}\left\{(h_n-\lVert x-b\rVert_2)_+
 +\Delta\phi\!\left(\frac{\lVert x-b\rVert_2}{\Delta}\right)
 \mathbf1\{\lVert x-b\rVert_2<\Delta\}\right\}.
\]
Given \(X\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

statements.statement: For every \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0\), both \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}\) and \(P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_L\), their released one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta\) are identical, and \(\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=2c_L\Delta\).
statements.justification: This certifies an exact order-\(\Delta\) alias in a legal uniform-half-disc subclass of the unknown-design point-anchored model, without asserting design-wide orthogonality.
statements.gap: Scalar rounding results do not furnish the radial-Jacobian null direction for a release that hides bivariate coordinates within annuli.
statements.consumer: Data stewards using released radial bins can see that no sample size removes the first-bin resolution floor.
statements.proof_tex:
The polynomial specified in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\) is
\[
 \phi(u)=1-3u+2u^2,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du
 =\int_0^1(u-3u^2+2u^3)\,du
 =\frac12-1+\frac12=0.
\]
Furthermore, \(\phi(1)=0\), \(|\phi(u)|\leq1\) for \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\phi'(u)=-3+4u\), whence \(\sup_{u\in[0,1]}|\phi'(u)|=3\).  Define
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}.
\]
Because the two pieces agree at \(r=\Delta\), the preceding derivative bound shows that \(a_\Delta\) is continuous and \(3\)-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  The radius map is \(1\)-Lipschitz, since
\[
 \bigl|\lVert x-b\rVert_2-\lVert x'-b\rVert_2\bigr|
 \leq\lVert x-x'\rVert_2.
\]

Consider either law in \(\mathrm{def:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\).  Choose the control anchor \(\theta_0=1/2\) and the treated anchor
\[
 \theta_{1,\pm}=\frac12\pm c_L\Delta
 =\frac12\pm c_La_\Delta(0).
\]
For every treated point \(x\) with radius \(r\leq1/2\), the point-anchor deviation is
\[
 |\mu_{1,\pm}(x)-\theta_{1,\pm}|
 =c_L|a_\Delta(r)-a_\Delta(0)|
 \leq3c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(c_L\leq L/8\).  The corresponding control deviation is zero.  Also
\[
 |c_La_\Delta(r)|\leq c_L\Delta
 \leq\frac1{16}\frac14=\frac1{64},
\]
using \(c_L\leq1/16\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\); hence all constructed Bernoulli means lie in \([0,1]\).  Thus the Bernoulli and point-anchor member conditions hold.

The construction supplies the known half-plane partition, sharp assignment, consistency, and conditionally Bernoulli potential outcomes.  Uniformity of \(X\) on the unit disc and polar integration give, for every \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)
 =\frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_t}\int_0^H r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{H^2}{2}
 \geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\Theta_t|=\pi,
\]
by \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Consequently both constructed laws are members of the unknown-design point-anchored class \(\mathcal P_L\).  This verifies membership through an embedded uniform-half-disc subclass only; it does not assert the alias identity for an arbitrary design in \(\mathcal P_L\).

The distribution of \((T,Q_\Delta(R))\) is common to the two signs.  Within the treated first bin, the difference of their joint success masses is
\[
 \frac1\pi\int_{\Theta_1}\int_0^\Delta
 2c_L\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)r\,dr\,d\vartheta
 =2c_L\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
Outside this bin the perturbation vanishes, and every control cell is unchanged.  Since \(Y\) is binary, equality of each released cell's total mass and success mass also gives equality of its failure mass.  Hence the entire one-unit laws of \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\) coincide.  Finally, by \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) and \(\phi(0)=1\),
\[
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{+,\Delta}}(b)=c_L\Delta,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P^{\mathrm{alias}}_{-,\Delta}}(b)=-c_L\Delta,
\]
so their difference is \(2c_L\Delta\), as claimed.

statements.statement: Can one derive from \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\), for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), a single pair \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) whose released product laws have total-variation distance at most a constant \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) and whose target separation is at least \(c(h_n+\Delta)\), with constants independent of \(n\) and \(\Delta\)?
statements.justification: A single regime-uniform pair is the genuinely open step needed to make the sampling and aliasing difficulties coexist rather than appear as unrelated lower bounds.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance supplies a localized exact-radius testing move, and the first-bin alias supplies zero grouped likelihood change, but no source combines them under one Bernoulli range and one Lipschitz budget.
statements.consumer: Resolving the question supplies the lower-bound engine for both minimax risk and honest expected length at the transition \(\Delta\asymp n^{-1/4}\).

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(L\), \(c_0\), and \(\Delta_0\), such that for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}\leq\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}\) and \(c\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\leq\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}\leq C\rho_{n,\Delta}^2\). The upper bounds are attained, up to \(C\), by \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: This is the sampling--quantization minimax frontier over the unknown-design bivariate Lipschitz boundary class.
statements.gap: Exact-radius boundary methods and ordinary scalar rounding methods do not derive the latent-annular rate \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) over this superclass.
statements.consumer: The result tells users of the \(\texttt{rd2d}\) R, Python, and Stata workflows when the Ser Pilo Paga analysis is sample-limited or release-precision-limited.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{n,\Delta}\).  From \(H=\Delta\lceil h/\Delta\rceil\), \(n\geq256\), and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\),
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho,
 \qquad 0<H\leq\frac12.
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Use \(A_t,q_t,\nu_t,N_t,S_t\) from \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\).  That lemma and the definition \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\) give
\[
 q_t\geq c_0H^2,
 \qquad |\nu_t-\theta_t|\leq LH,
 \qquad N_t\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
 \qquad S_t\mid N_t=k\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
In particular, \(0\leq\nu_t\leq1\).

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\) with \(q>0\), integrating its probability generating function gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{n+1}}{(n+1)q}
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Since \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\) for \(k\geq1\), and then by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]
 \leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}}.
\]
Also \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\).  The elementary inequalities \(x^{1/2}e^{-x}\leq1\) and \(xe^{-x}\leq1\) for \(x>0\) imply
\[
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq(nq)^{-1}.
\]

On \(N_t=k>0\), clipping does nothing because \(0\leq S_t/k\leq1\).  The ratio has conditional mean \(\nu_t\) and variance \(\nu_t(1-\nu_t)/k\leq1/(4k)\).  On \(N_t=0\), the fixed fallback obeys
\[
 |1/2-\nu_t|\leq\frac12,
 \qquad (1/2-\nu_t)^2\leq\frac14,
\]
which uses only the full Bernoulli range \([0,1]\).  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and the inverse-count bounds therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t|
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{\frac2{nq_t}}
      +\frac1{2\sqrt{nq_t}}
 =\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)\frac1{\sqrt{nq_t}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\nu_t)^2]
 \leq\frac14\frac2{nq_t}+\frac14\frac1{nq_t}
 =\frac3{4nq_t}.
\]
Adding the point-anchor bias and using \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t|
 \leq LH+\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12\right)
              \frac1{\sqrt{c_0nH^2}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}-\theta_t)^2]
 \leq2L^2H^2+\frac3{2c_0nH^2}.
\]
Since \(H\geq h=n^{-1/4}\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho^2.
\]
The identity \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), the triangle inequality, and \((x-y)^2\leq2x^2+2y^2\) now imply constants \(C_1,C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(L\) and \(c_0\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b)|\leq C_1\rho,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}-\tau_P(b))^2]\leq C_2\rho^2.
\]
The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\), and the zero-count branch is fixed, so \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}\) is one law-independent member of \(\mathcal T_{n,\Delta}\).  Taking the infima in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risks}\) proves both upper bounds.

For the converse, use the pair in \(\mathrm{thm:single\text{-}joint\text{-}pair}\).  Its two laws belong to the embedded uniform-half-disc subclass and hence to the unknown-design point-anchored superclass.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be their released product laws, let \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\) be their targets, and set \(\delta=|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|\).  The theorem gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 \delta=\kappa(h+\Delta)\geq\kappa\rho,
 \qquad \kappa=\frac{c_L}{4}>0.
\]
For any released-data estimator \(a\), take densities \(q_0,q_1\) with respect to \(Q_0+Q_1\).  Pointwise,
\[
 |a-\vartheta_0|+|a-\vartheta_1|\geq\delta,
 \qquad
 (a-\vartheta_0)^2+(a-\vartheta_1)^2\geq\frac{\delta^2}{2},
\]
and \(\int\min(q_0,q_1)=1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\).  Multiplying by the minimum density, integrating, and bounding a maximum below by half the sum give
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|a-\vartheta_j|
 \geq\frac\delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa}{8}\rho,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}(a-\vartheta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
 \geq\frac{3\kappa^2}{16}\rho^2.
\]
The supremum over \(\mathcal P_L\) dominates the maximum over this pair.  Taking the infimum over estimators proves the lower bounds.  Choose \(c\) as the smaller of the two displayed lower constants and choose \(C\) larger than \(c\), \(C_1\), and \(C_2\).  This proves the simultaneous assertion with the allowed dependence on \(L,c_0,\Delta_0\).

statements.statement: For every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), the interval \(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) is defined for every released sample, satisfies \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb P_P(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})\geq1-\alpha\), and obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]\leq C_{L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: Conditional-count exact inversion plus sidewise Euclidean Lipschitz enlargement yields a total honest interval under unknown design.
statements.gap: Existing ordinary-running-variable intervals do not handle latent annuli, quadratic local mass, or empty random side counts in this release field.
statements.consumer: The interval is directly implementable as a safe fallback in quantized \(\texttt{rd2d.dist}\) workflows.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), and write
\[
 h=h_n=n^{-1/4},\qquad H=H_{n,\Delta},\qquad B=LH.
\]
The aligned-bandwidth definition gives
\[
 h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12,
\]
because \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}local\text{-}binomial\text{-}law}\) gives
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0,
 \qquad
 \nu_t:=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid T=t,R<H],
\]
\[
 |\nu_t-\theta_t|=|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH=B,
 \qquad
 N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t),
\]
and, for every count value \(k\) having positive probability,
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid\{N_{t,n,\Delta}=k\}
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t).
\]
The equality between rounded and unrounded localization used here is exact because
\[
 \{Q_\Delta(R)<H\}
 =\{\Delta\lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<K_{n,\Delta}\Delta\}
 =\{R<H\}.
\]

If \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=0\), the side interval is \([0,1]\) and contains \(\nu_t\).  If the count is \(k>0\), the revalidated cited leaf \(\mathrm{lem:clopper\text{-}pearson\text{-}conditional\text{-}coverage}\), applied to the conditional binomial law, gives conditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha/2\).  Averaging over the count gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\{\nu_t\in[\ell_t,u_t]\}\geq1-\alpha/2.
\]
By a union bound there is an event \(E\) of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on which both side inclusions hold.  On \(E\),
\[
 \nu_1-\nu_0\in[\ell_1-u_0,u_1-\ell_0]
\]
and the two point-anchor bias inequalities imply
\[
 |\tau_P(b)-(\nu_1-\nu_0)|
 =|(\theta_1-\nu_1)-(\theta_0-\nu_0)|
 \leq2B.
\]
Thus \(\tau_P(b)\in C_{n,\Delta,\alpha}\) on \(E\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_L\).

The counts and successes are measurable functions of \(Z_\Delta^n\); the Clopper--Pearson endpoints are functions on a finite count-success state space; and the zero-count branch is explicit.  Since \(0\leq\ell_t\leq u_t\leq1\) and \(B<\infty\), the endpoints in \(\mathrm{def:total\text{-}honest\text{-}interval}\) form an ordered, closed, bounded, \(\sigma(Z_\Delta^n)\)-measurable interval on every sample.  This proves totality and honesty.

For expected length, put \(\beta=\alpha/4>0\).  Fix \(k\geq1\), \(s\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\), set \(\widehat p=s/k\), and write
\[
 I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(s)=[\ell,u].
\]
For a nontrivial upper endpoint, let \(d=u-\widehat p>0\) and \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,u)\).  On \(\{W\leq s\}\), \(|W-ku|\geq kd\), so the upper endpoint equation in the cited leaf and the binomial variance identity yield
\[
 \beta=\mathbb P_u(W\leq s)
 \leq\frac{u(1-u)}{kd^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p+d}{kd^2}.
\]
Thus \(d^2\leq \widehat p/(k\beta)+d/(k\beta)\).  If nonnegative numbers satisfy \(d^2\leq A+Dd\), then either \(d\leq D\), or \((d-D)^2\leq d(d-D)\leq A\); in both cases \(d\leq\sqrt A+D\).  Therefore
\[
 u-\widehat p\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
For a nontrivial lower endpoint, set \(d_-=\widehat p-\ell>0\) and take \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\ell)\).  On \(\{W\geq s\}\), \(|W-k\ell|\geq kd_-\).  The lower endpoint equation and \(\ell(1-\ell)\leq\ell\leq\widehat p\) give
\[
 \beta\leq\frac{\ell(1-\ell)}{kd_-^2}
 \leq\frac{\widehat p}{kd_-^2},
 \qquad
 \widehat p-\ell\leq\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}.
\]
The cited boundary conventions cover \(s=0\) and \(s=k\), so for every \(s\),
\[
 u-\ell\leq2\sqrt{\frac{\widehat p}{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k>0\), Jensen's inequality and \(0\leq S_{t,n,\Delta}/k\leq1\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k]
 \leq\frac2{\sqrt{k\beta}}+\frac1{k\beta}.
\]

For \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\), \(q>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac1{N+1}\right]
 =\int_0^1(1-q+qx)^n\,dx
 \leq\frac1{(n+1)q}.
\]
Using \(k^{-1}\leq2(k+1)^{-1}\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and \((1-q)^n\leq e^{-nq}\leq(nq)^{-1}\), one obtains
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}N\right]\leq\frac2{nq},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1\{N>0\}}{\sqrt N}\right]\leq\sqrt{\frac2{nq}},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(N=0)\leq\frac1{nq}.
\]
The zero-count side interval has length one.  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P[u_t-\ell_t]
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta nq_t}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{nq_t}
 \leq\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0nH^2}}
 +\left(1+\frac2\beta\right)\frac1{c_0nH^2}.
\]

The constructed interval has exact length
\[
 \operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})
 =(u_1-\ell_1)+(u_0-\ell_0)+4LH.
\]
Finally,
\[
 H<h+\Delta\leq2\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{\sqrt nH}\leq h\leq\rho_{n,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \frac1{nH^2}\leq h^2\leq\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
Summing the two side bounds gives, with \(\beta=\alpha/4\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\Delta,\alpha})]
 \leq
 \left\{
 \frac{4\sqrt2}{\sqrt{\beta c_0}}
 +\frac{2(1+2/\beta)}{c_0}+8L
 \right\}\rho_{n,\Delta}.
\]
This finite constant has the permitted dependence on \(L,c_0,\alpha,\Delta_0\) and is uniform in every allowed \(n\) and \(\Delta\).

statements.statement: There is a constant \(c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), every \(C\in\mathcal C_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_L}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C)]\geq c_{L,\alpha,\Delta_0}\rho_{n,\Delta}\); hence \(\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\asymp\rho_{n,\Delta}\).
statements.justification: The expected-length lower bound certifies that the total interval pays exactly the information loss forced by the release protocol.
statements.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal gives general modulus lower bounds and KolesarRothe2018Discrete gives discrete-RD intervals, but neither evaluates the rounded radial modulus or its \(n^{-1/4}\)-to-\(\Delta\) transition.
statements.consumer: The lower bound provides a performance certificate for software defaults and prevents misleading interval comparisons that ignore impossible within-bin recovery.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\ge256\) and \(0<\Delta\le\Delta_0\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{n,\Delta}\) admits one same-class baseline--alternative realization with both difficulties present.  Specifically, put \(\kappa=c_L/4\), \(b_h(r)=(h_n-r)_+\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf 1\{0\le r<\Delta\},
 \qquad
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}.
\]
There are \(P_{0,n,\Delta},P_{1,n,\Delta}\in\mathcal P_L\) with \(m_{0,0}=m_{0,1}=1/2\), \(m_{1,0}=1/2\), and \(m_{1,1}=1/2+g_{n,\Delta}\), for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n),
 \mathcal L_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(Z_\Delta^n)\right)
 \le\frac14<1-2\alpha
\]
and
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =\kappa(h_n+\Delta).
\]
statements.justification: One legal uniform-half-disc pair combines the sampling bump and exact first-bin alias while charging released divergence only for the sampling component.
statements.gap: No cited comparator supplies a single pair for the latent annular experiment with both order-\(n^{-1/4}\) and order-\(\Delta\) displacement.
statements.consumer: The pair is the common lower certificate for absolute risk, squared risk, and honest expected interval length over the point-anchored superclass.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq256\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and abbreviate \(h=h_n\) and \(\kappa=c_L/4\).  Then \(h\leq1/4\) and \(\Delta\leq1/4\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:first\text{-}bin\text{-}alias}\),
\[
 a_\Delta(r)=\Delta\phi(r/\Delta)\mathbf1\{0\leq r<\Delta\}
\]
is \(3\)-Lipschitz, satisfies \(a_\Delta(0)=\Delta\), and has the exact null moment
\[
 \int_0^\Delta ra_\Delta(r)\,dr
 =\Delta^3\int_0^1u\phi(u)\,du=0.
\]
The function \(b_h(r)=(h-r)_+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz and has \(b_h(0)=h\).  Therefore
\[
 g_{n,\Delta}(r)=\kappa\{b_h(r)+a_\Delta(r)\}
\]
is \(4\kappa=c_L\leq L\)-Lipschitz and
\[
 |g_{n,\Delta}(r)|
 \leq\kappa(h+\Delta)
 \leq\frac{c_L}{8}
 \leq\frac1{128}<\frac12.
\]

Take the laws named in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}lower\text{-}handle}\).  Under \(P_{0,n,\Delta}\), choose both boundary anchors equal to \(1/2\).  Under \(P_{1,n,\Delta}\), choose \(\theta_0=1/2\) and
\[
 \theta_1=\frac12+g_{n,\Delta}(0)
 =\frac12+\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]
The displayed range bound places all conditional Bernoulli means in \([0,1]\).  For any treated point of radius \(r\leq1/2\), the reverse triangle inequality and the Lipschitz bound give
\[
 |\mu_1(x)-\theta_1|
 =|g_{n,\Delta}(r)-g_{n,\Delta}(0)|
 \leq c_Lr\leq Lr,
\]
while all other point-anchor deviations are zero.  The construction supplies the known sharp half-plane partition, consistency, and conditional Bernoulli laws.  Uniform polar integration gives, for each side and \(0<H\leq1/2\),
\[
 \mathbb P(T=t,R<H)=\frac{H^2}{2}\geq c_0H^2,
\]
because \(c_0\leq1/2\).  Thus both laws belong to the unknown-design point-anchored superclass \(\mathcal P_L\); uniform-half-disc structure is used only to certify this embedded subclass.  Their target separation is
\[
 \tau_{P_{1,n,\Delta}}(b)-\tau_{P_{0,n,\Delta}}(b)
 =g_{n,\Delta}(0)=\kappa(h+\Delta).
\]

It remains to control the distance between released laws.  Partition \([0,1]\) into the positive-mass quantizer cells \(A_j=[j\Delta,\min\{(j+1)\Delta,1\})\), and define
\[
 w_j=\int_{A_j}r\,dr,
 \qquad
 \overline b_j=w_j^{-1}\int_{A_j}rb_h(r)\,dr.
\]
For the uniform disc cut into half-discs,
\[
 w_j=\mathbb P(T=1,Q_\Delta(R)=j\Delta).
\]
The alias term is supported in the complete first cell and has zero \(r\)-weighted integral there, while it vanishes in every other cell.  Thus, cell by cell, the treated conditional success probability is \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+\kappa\overline b_j\) under \(P_1\); all control cells agree.

Let \(Q_k=\mathcal L_{P_k}(Z_\Delta)\).  Direct summation over the two Bernoulli outcomes gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+x),
                    \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\right)=4x^2.
\]
Consequently, Jensen's inequality within each quantizer cell yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d:=\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=4\kappa^2\sum_jw_j\overline b_j^{,2}\\
 &\leq4\kappa^2\int_0^1rb_h(r)^2\,dr
 =4\kappa^2\int_0^h r(h-r)^2\,dr
 =\frac{\kappa^2h^4}{3}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Independent sampling makes the likelihood ratio a product.  Expanding its second moment and using \(nh^4=1\) gives
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+d)^n
 \leq\exp(nd)
 \leq\exp(\kappa^2/3).
\]
Since \(\kappa=c_L/4\leq1/64\), the elementary inequality \(e^x-1\leq2x\) for \(0\leq x\leq1\) implies
\[
 \chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{3}.
\]
Writing \(M=dQ_1^{\otimes n}/dQ_0^{\otimes n}\), Cauchy--Schwarz now gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}|M-1|
 \leq\frac12\{\mathbb E_{Q_0^{\otimes n}}(M-1)^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt6}<\frac14.
\]
Finally \(\alpha<1/4\) implies \(1/4<1-2\alpha\).  This establishes the proposed statement's same-class realization, separation, and uniform total-variation bound.

statements.statement:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), \(n\geq256\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  For every event \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) with \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\),
\[
 Y\mid B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B]\right).
\]
In particular, put \(A_t=\{T=t,Q_\Delta(R)<H_{n,\Delta}\}\).  Then \(A_t=\{T=t,R<H_{n,\Delta}\}\), its probability \(q_t\) is at least \(c_0H_{n,\Delta}^2>0\), and, with
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t],
\]
one has \(|\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|\leq LH_{n,\Delta}\), \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\), and
\[
 S_{t,n,\Delta}\mid N_{t,n,\Delta}=k
 \sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\text{ with }\mathbb P_P(N_{t,n,\Delta}=k)>0.
\]
statements.justification: This lemma supplies the conditional-count likelihood and the explicit point-anchor bias uniformly over unknown bivariate designs.
statements.gap: Exact-radius and scalar-running-variable analyses do not state the conditional Bernoulli law after retaining only side and quantized radius under an unknown bivariate design.
statements.consumer: The count law is the implementation contract for the bin-aware estimator and the total confidence interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(B\in\sigma(T,Q_\Delta(R))\) satisfy \(B\subseteq\{T=t\}\) and \(\mathbb P_P(B)>0\).  Consistency gives \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(B\).  The conditional Bernoulli member condition and iterated conditioning therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb P_P(Y=1\mid B)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbb P_P(Y(t)=1\mid X)\mid B\right]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid B].
\]
As \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), its conditional law is determined by this success probability, proving the first assertion.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}anchor\text{-}uniqueness}\) ensures that the declared \(\theta_t=\mu_t(b)\) is a well-defined functional of the law rather than a choice of regression version.

Put \(h=h_n\), \(H=H_{n,\Delta}\), and \(K=K_{n,\Delta}\).  Since \(H=K\Delta\), the floor quantizer satisfies, pointwise on \([0,1]\),
\[
 Q_\Delta(R)<H
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \lfloor R/\Delta\rfloor<K
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R<K\Delta=H.
\]
Moreover, \(n\geq256\) and \(\Delta\leq\Delta_0\leq1/4\) give
\[
 0<h=n^{-1/4}\leq\frac14,
 \qquad h\leq H<h+\Delta\leq\frac12.
\]
Thus the two-sided local-mass member condition applies and yields
\[
 q_t:=\mathbb P_P(A_t)
 =\mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)
 \geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
The first part of the proof with \(B=A_t\) shows that \(Y\mid A_t\) is Bernoulli with parameter
\[
 \nu_t=\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)\mid A_t].
\]
The point-anchored envelope applies \(P_X\)-almost surely throughout \(A_t\).  Using \(\mu_t(b)=\theta_t\), conditional Jensen's inequality for absolute value, and \(R<H\) on \(A_t\), one obtains
\[
 |\nu_t-\mu_t(b)|
 =|\mathbb E_P[\mu_t(X)-\theta_t\mid A_t]|
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|\mu_t(X)-\theta_t|\mid A_t]
 \leq L\mathbb E_P[R\mid A_t]
 \leq LH.
\]

By independent identical sampling, the pairs
\[
 \left(\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\},\mathbf1\{A_{t,i}\}Y_i\right),
 \qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
are iid.  Hence \(N_{t,n,\Delta}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q_t)\).  Their one-unit joint probability generating function, with \(w\) marking local membership and \(z\) marking a success, is
\[
 1-q_t+q_t(1-\nu_t)w+q_t\nu_twz.
\]
After taking the \(n\)-th power, the coefficient of \(w^k\) is proportional to \((1-\nu_t+\nu_tz)^k\).  Conditional on every count value \(k\) of positive probability, this is the probability generating function of \(\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\nu_t)\), proving the final assertion, including the degenerate case \(k=0\).

statements.statement: For every integer \(k\geq1\), if \(S\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,p)\), then the equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(S)\) covers \(p\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\).  Writing \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{k,\alpha/2}(s)=[\ell,u]\), its boundary conventions are \(\ell=0\) at \(s=0\) and \(u=1\) at \(s=k\); with \(\beta=\alpha/4\), the non-boundary endpoints satisfy \(\mathbb P_{\ell}\{W\geq s\}=\beta\) and \(\mathbb P_u\{W\leq s\}=\beta\) for \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\ell)\) and \(W\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,u)\), respectively.

source.locator: pp. 406--407, inversion of the two binomial tails defining the fiducial limits
source.verbatim_statement: not more than 2½% on or above the upper boundary and not more than 2½% on or below the lower boundary.

attestation.note: Verified against the public JSTOR scan of Clopper and Pearson (1934), Biometrika 26(4), pp. 404-413, hosted at https://www.barestatistics.nl/uploads/1/1/7/9/11797954/clopper__pearson_1934.pdf; inspected original pp. 406-407. DOI and bibliographic identity cross-checked against Oxford Academic DOI 10.1093/biomet/26.4.404 and CiNii OUP metadata.

statements.justification: The total interval uses exact conditional binomial inversion rather than an asymptotic normal approximation.
statements.gap: This classical leaf supplies only binomial coverage and endpoint equations; the random-count and spatial-bias adaptation is proved in this note.
statements.consumer: The endpoint equations yield both finite-sample coverage and the expected-width calculation.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), there is at most one \(a\in[0,1]\) such that \(|\mu_t(x)-a|\leq L\lVert x-b\rVert_2\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\lVert x-b\rVert_2\leq1/2\). Consequently, the declared \(\theta_t\) and \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) are well-defined functionals of \(P\).
statements.justification: The point anchor must be a functional of the law, not an arbitrary version choice, for the boundary contrast to be a well-defined causal estimand.
statements.gap: The uniqueness step is specific to combining an almost-everywhere point envelope with positive side mass at every shrinking radius.
statements.consumer: All risk and coverage statements use the uniquely determined boundary anchor contrast.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_L\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  Suppose \(a,a'\in[0,1]\) each satisfies the displayed point-anchor envelope.  For any \(H\in(0,1/2]\), the local-mass member condition gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P(T=t,R<H)\geq c_0H^2>0.
\]
Each candidate envelope holds outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of the side-\(t\), radius-at-most-\(1/2\) region.  Removing the union of those two null sets from \(\{T=t,R<H\}\) leaves a nonempty set.  At any \(x\) in that set,
\[
 |a-a'|
 \leq|a-\mu_t(x)|+|\mu_t(x)-a'|
 \leq2L\lVert x-b\rVert_2
 <2LH.
\]
This holds for every \(H\in(0,1/2]\).  Taking \(H\downarrow0\) gives \(|a-a'|=0\), hence \(a=a'\).  Existence of the declared anchor is part of the class construction, so it is unique for each side.  Therefore \(\theta_t\), and hence \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\), is a well-defined functional of \(P\).

statements.statement: Along every sequence with \(0<\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the unknown-design frontier has minimax absolute-error and honest expected-length order \(n^{-1/4}\) and squared-risk order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Along every sequence with \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), the corresponding orders are \(\Delta\) and \(\Delta^2\), respectively.
statements.justification: This separates the fine-quantization sampling regime from the coarsening-dominated regime without claiming equivalence to an exact-score theorem.
statements.gap: The exact-score literature is a rate sanity check only; it does not imply the latent-annular experiment proved here.
statements.consumer: Applied users can diagnose whether sample size or released radial precision is the active constraint.

sampling_model.design: Independent uniform sampling on the known unit disc centered at \(b\), split into two equal half-discs by the known normal \(e_1\).
sampling_model.units: \((X_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed; the raw locations are latent after release.
sampling_model.treatment: Sharp deterministic assignment \(T_i=\mathbf1\{e_1^{\top}(X_i-b)\geq0\}\), with consistency for \(Y_i\).
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is imposed because assignment is deterministic; both geometric sides have known probability \(1/2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No design-density nuisance is estimated. The procedure uses only \(Z_{\Delta,i}=(Y_i,T_i,Q_\Delta(R_i))\), the known probability \(p_{n,\Delta}=H_{n,\Delta}^2/2\), and the known smoothness envelope \(L\).

estimand_functional: For the causal target \(\tau_P(b)=\theta_1-\theta_0\) over the unknown-design point-anchored class \(\mathcal P_L\), \(\widehat\tau_{n,\Delta}=\widehat m_{1,n,\Delta}-\widehat m_{0,n,\Delta}\), where \(\widehat m_{t,n,\Delta}=\Pi_{[0,1]}(S_{t,n,\Delta}/N_{t,n,\Delta})\) on \(N_{t,n,\Delta}>0\) and equals \(1/2\) otherwise; \(\mathfrak R^{(1)}_{n,\Delta}\asymp\mathfrak W_{n,\Delta}(\alpha)\asymp\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) and \(\mathfrak R^{(2)}_{n,\Delta}\asymp\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}^2\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Provides exact-observed-coordinate distance-based rate and method benchmarks under a different smoothness class; it does not prove the unknown-design latent-annular point-anchor experiment here.
Studies rounding of an ordinary scalar running variable under moment structure, not loss of raw bivariate coordinates within radial annuli or the radial-Jacobian null direction.
Develops inference for an ordinary discrete running variable, not total conditional-count inference with unknown bivariate design, quadratic local mass, and latent within-annulus bias.
Supplies general modulus logic but does not evaluate the rounded radial modulus or construct the single sampling-plus-aliasing pair used for this point-anchored superclass.
Supplies the bias-enlargement principle, while the present random-count exact-binomial interval and all-regime expected-length bound are specific to this release experiment.
Studies causal targets compatible with correctly classified coarsened running scores; it does not recover the fixed latent boundary anchor contrast from side and rounded radius alone.

tldr: A boundary-discontinuity analyst receives treatment side, Bernoulli outcome, and floor-rounded point-radius, but no angle, raw radius, or raw coordinate. In the uniform two-sided half-disc benchmark, the effective local mass inside radius \(h\) is order \(h^2\), producing the pointwise sampling scale \(n^{-1/4}\). Floor rounding creates a second, exact information loss: the first-bin direction \(\phi(u)=(1-u)(1-2u)\) has zero mean under the radial Jacobian \(u\,du\), yet shifts the boundary limit by order \(\Delta\). The proposal derives one regime-uniform least-favorable pair combining these two moves, proves absolute minimax risk and honest expected length of order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\), proves squared risk of the corresponding squared order, and supplies a total bin-aware estimator and exact-binomial interval with explicit Lipschitz bias.

project_justification.gap: Exact-distance boundary theory and ordinary one-score rounding theory leave open the statistical experiment created when a fixed boundary point is represented only by treatment side and floor-rounded radial distance.
project_justification.niche: The radial Jacobian makes first-bin aliasing different from scalar RD rounding, while the probability of a useful local bin is quadratic in its radius. This creates a sampling--resolution transition not covered by either literature.
project_justification.fill: The project fixes the release \(\sigma\)-field, derives its grouped Bernoulli likelihood, constructs a bin-aligned inverse-probability estimator and a total exact-binomial interval, and asks for one same-class testing pair that certifies the joint \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\) frontier uniformly across quantization regimes.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the writing and sampling-method anchor: its Introduction treats point-distance as deliberate information reduction, Theorem 4 gives the \(1/(nh^2)\) pointwise stochastic scale, Theorem 6 gives an exact-radius isotropic minimax limitation, and its Conclusion points toward procedures that incorporate additional geometric information. The first changed step here is replacing exact-radius kernel moments and likelihoods by annular cell averages. Dong2015Rounding is the identification-method anchor: Theorem 1 integrates latent scalar scores over rounding cells and inverts a polynomial moment map when rounding moments are known. Its proof uses iterated expectations and a triangular moment matrix; here the radial Jacobian instead exposes a nonparametric within-cell null direction. KolesarRothe2018Discrete shows that clustering by support value does not control specification bias and constructs honest smoothness-based alternatives, but its support probabilities are those of an ordinary scalar running variable and its Proposition 1 does not address empty radial bins or latent annular bias. ArmstrongKolesar2018Optimal supplies the convex-class modulus logic for turning the same pair into risk and expected-length lower bounds. ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest supplies the estimator-centered inference move of adding an explicit worst-case bias envelope, while the present interval uses exact binomial inversion to remain total on sparse-count events. DongKolesar2023Measurement clarifies that correctly classified coarsened scores can target effects conditional on the observed score; that target is not the fixed latent boundary effect studied here. KeeleTitiunik2015Geographic explains why the retained spatial coordinate is part of the estimand, and CattaneoTitiunikYu2025Rd2d documents the R, Python, and Stata workflows that consume the proposed correction.
technical_internal_limitation: The half-disc benchmark deliberately makes the radial cell law known and common across sides. The rate theorem does not claim transfer to curved boundaries or unknown nonuniform design densities. In those models, the polynomial \(\phi\) need not be orthogonal to the latent first-bin weight, and raw locations would permit estimation of that weight; neither fact is available under the present release field.
honest_scope: The theorem-level target is rate sharpness, not a sharp leading constant. The estimator and interval exploit the known uniform design probability, while the outcome regressions remain nonparametric Lipschitz functions. The open content is the single joint lower pair and its conversion to an honest expected-length lower bound. When \(\Delta\leq n^{-1/4}\), the result reduces to the familiar pointwise radial Lipschitz scale \(n^{-1/4}\); when \(n^{-1/4}=o(\Delta)\), exact first-bin aliasing fixes the order-\(\Delta\) floor. If raw \(X\), polar angle together with within-bin radius, or raw \(R\) remains available, this proposal's observation model does not apply.
